title: Bite-Time vs Conditions Correlation
dataSources: Fishing catches (`fishing:catch`), fishfinder sonar (`fishfinder:reading`), foraging finds (`foraging:find`), game-cam triggers (`gamecam:trigger`).
app: Outdoor logs — fishing apps (Fishbrain), sonar / fishfinder exports, game/trail cameras, and foraging journals — streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal (sourcetype=fishing:catch OR sourcetype=ecowitt:obs)
| bin _time span=1h
| stats sum(eval(if(sourcetype=="fishing:catch",1,0))) as catches, avg(pressure_hpa) as pressure by _time
| eval falling=if(pressure<1010,"low/falling","high")
| stats avg(catches) as avg_catches by falling
description: Correlates your catch rate with barometric pressure and time of day to learn when the fish really bite.
value: The old wisdom that fish bite on a falling barometer becomes testable against your own logged results.
implementation: Join catches with weather in `index=personal`; compare catch rate by pressure trend.
visualization: Bar chart of catch rate by barometric condition.
grandmaExplanation: It works out when the fish actually bite for you, based on weather and time of day.
